events.title: The Great Migration: An AI-Assisted Journey from TypeScript to Python
events.description:
Migrating an application from one programming language to another has traditionally been a time-consuming and risky process. But what changes when AI becomes part of the development team?
DSM Web Geeks welcomes Daryle Foulke on Monday, September 14th from 6:30-8pm for a look at migrating a TypeScript application to Python with modern AI coding assistants. Through a live demonstration, Daryle will walk through the migration process, showing where AI can accelerate the translation of business logic and application structure and where human expertise remains essential. He’ll also cover some of the challenges developers can encounter along the way, including type-system differences, package ecosystem mismatches, and async programming differences between Node.js and Python.
You’ll learn approaches for prompting AI coding assistants, validating generated code with tests, and breaking a migration into small, verifiable increments.

Speaker Bio: Daryle is a Software Engineer at Source Allies with experience across cloud technologies and full-stack development. His technical background includes AWS, Python, Java, TypeScript, GraphQL, Terraform, and PostgreSQL, along with experience building enterprise software and working directly with clients.

Event Details:
Monday, September 14th
6:30 to 8pm
Hosted at Source Allies and streamed online
Food and drinks provided for in-person attendees

events.title: Hacktoberfest
events.description:
Hacktoberfest 2026: DSM Web Geeks Hack Day

**Let’s get hacking!**
Join DSM Web Geeks on Monday, October 12th at 6:30 PM at Source Allies as we celebrate Hacktoberfest with an evening of open source, collaboration, and coding.

Hacktoberfest is a celebration of open source that brings developers together to contribute, learn, and support the projects and communities that make so much of modern software possible. Whether you’ve contributed to dozens of open source projects or have never opened a pull request before, you’re welcome to join us.

**What’s Happening?**
We’ll kick things off with a quick introduction to contributing to open source, including how to find a project, choose an issue, and work through the contribution and pull request process.

*Then we’ll start hacking!*

Bring your laptop and a project you’d like to contribute to, or join up with other developers at the event. We’ll have time to work individually, pair with others, ask questions, and share what we’re working on.

Have an open source project of your own that could use some help? Bring it! We’d love to give local maintainers a chance to introduce their projects and connect with potential contributors.

You don’t need to be an open source expert to participate. Documentation improvements, bug fixes, tests, accessibility improvements, and small features can all be valuable contributions. This is a chance to learn the contribution process in a friendly environment and meet other developers along the way.

**What to Bring**
Bring a laptop and anything else you need to code comfortably. If you already have a GitHub account, make sure you can log in before the event.

Don’t have a project in mind? That’s okay. We’ll help you find something to work on when you arrive.

*Food and drinks will be provided.*

events.title: What a Grasshopper Taught Me About Listening to Customers
events.description:
**What a Grasshopper Taught Me About Listening to Customers**

*Monday\, November 9th \| 6:30–8:00 PM \| Source Allies*

We all say we listen to customers. But how often do we stop to question whether what we think we know is actually true?

When teams move quickly, assumptions can start sounding a lot like facts. Those assumptions can influence everything from product decisions to customer experience and business strategy.

At our November DSM Web Geeks meetup, Clair Williams-Vavra will share an unexpected lesson from building a food startup that changed how she approaches customer experience. It started with a grasshopper and led to a question she's carried into her work ever since: How do we know?

Drawing on experiences from both startups and large enterprises, Clair will explore three important aspects of understanding customers: balancing value and friction, gathering quality evidence, and recognizing the assumptions we may be making or protecting.

**About the Speaker**
Clair Williams-Vavra is the Chief Operating Officer at Strategic Innovation Consulting, where she leads business operations and builds the teams, systems, and processes that support growth and delivery for state government clients.

Previously, Clair helped lead enterprise customer experience strategy at a large financial services company, focusing on improvements that delivered meaningful customer value.

**Event Details**
*Date:* Monday, November 9th, 2026
*Time:* 6:30–8:00 PM
*Location:* Source Allies, Urbandale, IA
